--- title: "Declared versus assessed VAT debt by CNAE level, age, status and concentration" description: "How do size, concentration, payment and recovery differ between declared and assessed VAT (ICMS) debt? December 2025 legal entities, CNAE 2.3, aggregates only." date: 2026-10-31 jupyter: python3 --- **Data:** December 2025 snapshot of the legal-entity VAT (ICMS) extract. Payments are GARE amounts dated before 1 January 2026. No 2026 debt and no 2026 payment enter. Firm attributes come from the Receita Federal CNPJ registry already linked to these debtors. Activity uses the official IBGE CNAE-Subclasses 2.3 hierarchy (1,331 subclasses). **What is shown:** aggregates only. A cell with 1 to 4 firms is left blank in the detailed activity files. **Status:** exploration. These are the aggregates used by the declared-versus-assessed manuscript. The computation is `analyze.py` in the folder of the same name. This page reads those outputs and redraws the figures. ::: {.callout-warning title="The firm register is later than the debts"} Registration status, CNAE, size, place and firm age describe the firm as the register stands. They are not measured before the debt. A firm may be closed or unfit because of the debt. Recovery is payments before 1 January 2026 divided by the December 2025 stock. It is not an annual hazard. ::: ## Question How do size, concentration, payment and recovery differ between declared and assessed VAT (ICMS) debt? Declared is `ICMS Declarado`: tax the firm reported and did not pay. Assessed is `ICMS Autuação` plus `ICMS Autuação Simples Nacional`: tax fixed by an assessment. Fecoep and the GIA amendment stay out of the comparison. ## Measures Stock is the December 2025 value net of legal fees. The payment rate is the share of certificates with any GARE payment before 1 January 2026. Recovery is those payments divided by the December 2025 stock. Debt age runs from the enrolment date to 31 December 2025. Dates before 1960 are missing. Firm age runs from the establishment opening date. Dates before 1900 are missing. A firm is the 8-digit CNPJ root. A firm has repeated enrolments when it holds two or more certificates in the segment. The Lorenz curve orders positive-value certificates from smallest to largest. The Gini coefficient is one minus twice the area under that curve. The top 1 percent is the largest ceil(1 percent of N) positive-value certificates. The Mann-Whitney rank-biserial correlation is positive when a random assessed unit tends to exceed a random declared unit. Cramér's V is the effect size of the chi-square test on firm counts. Except for repeated enrolment, each firm is placed in the segment that holds more of its stock. The samples are large, so every p-value is 0 at floating-point precision. The effect size is the result. ## Population check ::: {#tbl-validation .cell tbl-cap='December 2025 legal-entity VAT (ICMS) certificates in the extract, against the published laboratory page where that page reports the same row.' execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
raw_type n_cda stock_bn published_n published_bn delta_n delta_bn

1 ICMS Autuação 58,724 311.253361 58725.0 311.253429 -1.0 -0.000068
2 ICMS Autuação Simples Nacional 818 0.145030 NaN NaN NaN NaN
3 ICMS Declarado 2,257,189 116.424184 NaN NaN NaN NaN
4 ICMS Fecoep 8,510 0.048362 NaN NaN NaN NaN
5 ICMS (all types) 2,325,277 427.880276 2325280.0 427.880344 -3.0 -0.000068
``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Legal-entity total: 2,325,277 certificates and R$427.880 billion. The published laboratory page reports 2,325,280 certificates and R$427.880 billion. The gap is 3 certificates and about R$68,000. Simples Nacional assessments: 818 certificates and R$0.145 billion, 0.05 percent of assessed stock, reported in the manuscript as 0.05 percent. Fecoep: 8,510 certificates and R$0.048 billion. GIA amendment: 36 certificates and R$0.009 billion. Both stay out of the segment comparison. Establishment match: 59,020 of 59,542 assessed certificates (99.1 percent) and 2,256,655 of 2,257,189 declared certificates (100.0 percent). More than 99 percent in each segment. The CNAE 2.3 file has 1,331 subclasses. Placeholder code 8888888 covers 808 certificates and is not an activity. ``` ::: ::: ## Size, payment and recovery Assessed debt is the value. Declared debt is the count. Declared debt is 97.4 percent of the two-segment certificates and 27.2 percent of the two-segment stock. Assessed debt is 72.8 percent of that stock and 2.6 percent of the certificates. ::: {#tbl-profile .cell tbl-cap='Declared and assessed VAT (ICMS) debt in December 2025.' execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

Recovery 4.73 percent and 0.48 percent. Declared share of the two segments: 97.4 percent of certificates and 27.2 percent of stock. Assessed share: 2.6 percent of certificates and 72.8 percent of stock. ``` ::: ::: ::: {#tbl-mw .cell tbl-cap='Mann-Whitney comparisons. A positive rank-biserial correlation means a random assessed unit tends to exceed a random declared unit. Stock uses positive values. Firm ages are stock-weighted. Every p-value is 0 at floating-point precision.' execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

Positive-value counts: 59,294 assessed certificates and 2,254,387 declared certificates. ``` ::: ::: Some payment is more common on assessed certificates (17.4 percent against 9.1 percent). Reais collected per real of stock are higher for declared debt (4.73 percent against 0.48 percent). ## Concentration and the 1 percent cut ::: {#cell-fig-lorenz .cell execution_count=5} ::: {#fig-lorenz .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` Lorenz curves of December 2025 stock, positive certificate values. Certificates are ordered from the smallest value to the largest. ::: ::: The pooled Gini coefficient is 0.946. Inside declared debt it is 0.839. Inside assessed debt it is 0.863. ::: {#tbl-top1 .cell tbl-cap='Upper tail of the pooled stock, and the same 1 percent cut inside each segment. Positive values only.' execution_count=6} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
Cut Book Certificates Share of stock (%)

6 Largest 1 percent Declared 22,544 39.5
7 Largest 1 percent Assessed 593 39.9
``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Pooled top 1 percent: 23,137 certificates, 1.00 percent of the count, 75.8 percent of the stock. Gini 0.946. Largest half: 1,156,841 certificates hold 99.4 percent. Largest 10 percent: 231,369 certificates, 91.9 percent. Largest 5 percent: 115,685 certificates, 87.5 percent. Largest 0.5 percent: 11,569 certificates, 69.1 percent. Largest 0.1 percent: 2,314 certificates, 48.5 percent. Inside declared debt the largest 1 percent is 22,544 certificates and 39.5 percent of declared stock (Gini 0.839). Inside assessed debt it is 593 certificates and 39.9 percent of assessed stock (Gini 0.863). Of the 23,137 certificates in the pooled top 1 percent, 18,230 are assessed and hold 68.8 percent of the pooled stock. The other 4,907 are declared and hold 7.1 percent. A review list of about 23,000 certificates is the administrative reading of this cut. The cut describes where the stock sits. It is not evidence that collecting those certificates would recover the stock. ``` ::: ::: **Source.** December 2025 snapshot of the legal-entity VAT (ICMS) extract (`VALOR_SEM_HONORARIOS`), declared and assessed segments; CNAE section of the debtor establishment from the March 2026 Federal Revenue (RFB) register, CNAE 2.3 structure, establishment-level matches only. **Representation.** One row per segment × section (manufacturing, trade, transport, information); `n_positive` is the count of certificates (CDAs) with positive stock in that segment and section; the Gini coefficient and the share of the section's stock held by its largest 1 percent of certificates are computed on stock values inside each segment and section. **How to read.** A higher Gini or top-1 percent share means the section's stock sits in fewer certificates; compare the two segments within a section, not sections with the pooled figure. ::: {#tbl-section-concentration .cell tbl-cap='Gini coefficient and top 1 percent stock share inside the main CNAE sections.' execution_count=7} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

The Gini coefficients in those sections are about 0.82 to 0.87. That is not the pooled 75.8 percent. The pooled figure is the mixture of the two segments. ``` ::: ::: ## Age of the debt and age of the firm ::: {#cell-fig-age .cell execution_count=8} ::: {#fig-age .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

There is no 1 percent cut, no "All other sections" group, no payment or recovery rate, and no suppression. **How to read.** Bar length is that section's share of the segment's stock. Compare the declared and assessed bars of one section. Cramér's V for state is 0.15. The city of São Paulo holds 27.2 percent of assessed stock and 22.5 percent of declared stock. The city of Rio de Janeiro holds 7.8 percent of declared stock. Paulínia, with 215 firms, holds 4.9 percent of assessed stock. ``` ::: ::: **Rio de Janeiro in declared stock.** Rio de Janeiro is the second state in declared stock. That share comes from a small number of large debtors whose headquarters are in Rio de Janeiro and whose debt in São Paulo is small next to their stock in Rio. Without those debtors, Rio de Janeiro falls to about 0.3 percent of declared stock. The state is the address in the Federal Revenue (RFB) CNPJ registry of the certificate's CNPJ, not a field of the certificate. Whether these debts are ICMS-ST (tax substitution) or DIFAL (the interstate rate difference) owed to São Paulo cannot be tested with the current extract: no field separates them. The question stays open, pending confirmation from PGE. ## Repeated enrolment ::: {#cell-fig-repeated .cell execution_count=18} ::: {#fig-repeated .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Declared: 119,833 firms have two or more certificates. They are 67.4 percent of declared firms and hold 99.2 percent of declared stock. Assessed: 9,565 firms have two or more certificates. They are 31.9 percent of assessed firms and hold 82.3 percent of assessed stock. Cramér's V is 0.26 on 207,687 firm-segment rows. Separately, 11,928 firms hold at least one certificate in each segment. Firms with two or more certificates in either segment, counted once: 125,305. ``` ::: ::: ## What this does not show The register is observed after the debts, so closure and unfitness can be consequences. Certificate-level tests describe the portfolio. Certificates of the same firm are not independent, which is why the firm-level effect sizes are reported beside them. The 1 percent cut describes where the stock sits. It does not show that collecting those certificates would recover the stock. The evidence is a December 2025 cross-section, not a follow-up of each firm.
